clue.text: Stop avoiding right work in kitchen?

indicators.note: avoiding means the letter for right is kept out of the word for stop

parts.note: to brake is to stop a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop dodging proper work and get into the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking is a typical job done at the oven when cooking; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Fanciful of minister, say, to have him replacing a Liberal

indicators.note: replacing means the word him goes in where the letter for a Liberal stood

parts.note: clerical means relating to a minister or other member of the clergy
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A minister's fanciful idea of putting him in place of a Liberal colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping HIM for the first L of CLERICAL gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimerical describes something imaginary or wildly fanciful, like the mythical chimera.

clue.text: Contents of Asti carafe replaced — with a different wine

indicators.note: replaced means the remaining letters are put back in a new order
the contents of the phrase are everything inside its outer letters, so the first A and final E go

explanation.surface: The Asti in the carafe has been swapped for some other wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' strips the outer A and E from ASTI CARAFE, leaving STICARAF, which 'replaced' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Frascati is a white wine from the hills near Rome, distinct from the sparkling Asti of Piedmont.

clue.text: Salesman dodging repeat success

indicators.note: dodging means the salesman's word is left out of the longer word

parts.note: a reprise is a repeat of a piece of music or performance
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman who avoids making a second sale and still prospers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in the world, or a rise to fame, is a form of success.

clue.text: Look for attention in school

indicators.note: in means the word for attention sits inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A pupil seeking attention while at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to seek or hunt for something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: King's rule keeping up pace

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for rule is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a law is a rule
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king whose reign keeps up a steady pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' only joins the two pieces here: WAL is followed by K.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk is a pace or gait, as in a horse slowing to a walk.

clue.text: Dons casual pants, causing outrage

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of the two words are a mess to be sorted

explanation.surface: Someone wearing casual trousers and shocking everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers being put on; in British slang it also means poor or rubbish, hence the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scandalous provokes shock and public outrage.

clue.text: Almost crazy, that female swimmer

indicators.note: almost means the word for crazy loses its last letter

parts.note: bats is informal for crazy, as in bats in the belfry
her refers to a female person

explanation.surface: A woman in the water who is nearly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bather is someone who swims or bathes in the sea or a pool.

clue.text: Dean's speciality, getting one man enthralled by church repeatedly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: enthralled by means the man's name is held inside the doubled church letters
repeatedly means the abbreviation for church is written twice

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man named Dean whose special skill involves being captivated by church again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Dean, with Jayne Torvill, won Olympic gold for Britain in 1984 skating to Bolero.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Dean is famous for figure-skating partnerships on the rink, so this discipline is his specialism.

clue.text: Take off the blindfold and I'll offer some alternatives

definitions.meaning: a plea to be allowed to look
a filler phrase said while thinking of options

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a request to look at something and a stalling phrase while one considers possibilities.

clue.text: Monarch depicted by artist at an angle

indicators.note: depicted by means the monarch comes after the artist, as if painted by them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A king painted by an artist from an odd angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A raking stage or line slopes, so raking means set at a slant.

clue.text: Mountain dweller absolute in dismissing an English father

indicators.note: dismissing means one of the letters for English is sent away from the word for absolute

parts.note: sheer means absolute, as in sheer nonsense
E is the abbreviation for English
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A highlander utterly rejecting an English parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people living high in Nepal, famed as mountain guides.

clue.text: Honour aims when re-expressed? That's agreeable

indicators.note: re-expressed means the letters of the two words are said again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Restating one's honourable goals makes everyone content.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonious means in agreement, free of discord, so pleasant and agreeable.

clue.text: Had Prince dramatically recalled accepting Princess with a superior attitude?

indicators.note: accepting means the princess is taken in between the reversed pieces
recalled means the two words are called back, so read backwards

parts.note: Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Prince Henry in the Henry IV plays
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A prince in a play recalling a princess, with snobbish airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses HAD and HAL together to give LAHDAH; 'accepting' puts DI in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lah-di-dah describes affected, pretentious manners, putting on airs of superiority.

clue.text: Difficulty that's not soft or trivial

indicators.note: that's not means the letter for soft is removed from the word for difficulty

parts.note: a plight is a difficult situation
P is piano, the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A problem that is neither gentle nor petty.
explanation.definitionFit: Light reading or a light matter is unimportant, so light can mean trivial.

clue.text: Popular period to support dumping leader and to try unifying countries?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a term is a period of time

indicators.note: dumping leader means the first letter of the word for support is dropped

parts.note: to carry is to support a weight

explanation.surface: A popular spell of support, then an attempt to unite nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal houses long married into each other's families to bind kingdoms; the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynastic marriages between royal families were a classic way of forging alliances between nations.

clue.text: Cards inserted in pamphlet hurled into a radar establishment

indicators.note: inserted in means the cards are slipped inside the pamphlet

parts.note: a tract is a pamphlet, often religious
kings are playing cards

indicators.note: hurled means the letters of the two words are flung into a new order

explanation.surface: Cards slipped into a leaflet are thrown into a radar base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurled' looks like it governs the pamphlet; it rearranges INTO A to ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracking station uses radar and antennas to follow satellites, missiles or aircraft.

clue.text: Problematic mark of success is penned by left hand

parts.note: a tick marks a right answer

indicators.note: penned by means the word is is enclosed between the two abbreviations

explanation.surface: A tricky business: a tick of approval written by a left-handed person.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticklish situation is delicate or awkward, needing careful handling.

clue.text: Upright holy man behind sentimentality about upset pal

indicators.note: behind means the holy man follows the rest
about means the word for sentimentality goes around the rearranged pal

parts.note: goo is gushing sentimentality

indicators.note: upset means the letters of pal are knocked into a new order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint behind a soppy fuss over a distressed friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalpost is one of the two vertical posts of a goal, so an upright.

clue.text: Struggle of French in language exam?

indicators.note: in means the French word sits inside the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam, as in language tests
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A student wrestling with the French part of a speaking test.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or testing experience, a hard struggle.

clue.text: Light red coating everyone initially applied to 4

indicators.note: applied to means the first letters are attached to the front of the other answer
initially means the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: the answer to 4 down is rise

explanation.surface: A pale red coat put on everyone and applied to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is French for cherry and names a light cherry-red colour.

clue.text: Child keeping letter back is touched

indicators.note: keeping means the child holds the reversed letter inside

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: back means the name of the letter is read backwards

parts.note: ess is the spelt name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A child holding back a letter is emotionally moved.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kissed is to be touched by someone's lips.

clue.text: Place best for climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for best is read from the bottom up

parts.note: tops means the best, as in the tops

explanation.surface: The finest location for rock climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a place or location, as in a nice spot for a picnic.

clue.text: Folk-singing etc completely overwhelmed by dreadful lines

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the word for completely is swamped by the others around it

parts.note: bad means dreadful
all means completely, as in all alone
RY is short for railway lines

explanation.surface: Folk music utterly drowned out by awful verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Balladry is the composing and singing of ballads, a staple of folk tradition.

clue.text: Fish out of river is a ray

indicators.note: out of means the letter for river is taken out of the fish

parts.note: a bream is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish taken from the river turns out to be a ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like another fish; it means a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam of light is a ray, a narrow stream of it.

clue.text: Topless dress to startle

indicators.note: topless means the first letter, the top in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: A dress with no top would certainly shock people.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shake or shock them, as news can rock a nation.

clue.text: Robots running out in the morning, leading to American cheers

indicators.note: in means the rearranged word sits within the abbreviation for morning

parts.note: AM means in the morning

indicators.note: running means the letters of out are set in motion into another order

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Robots dashing out early and getting American applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is British for thanks, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata are self-operating machines, the older word for mechanical figures like robots.

clue.text: Collided with small lorry

parts.note: a truck is a lorry

explanation.surface: Hit by a little lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To have struck something is to have hit it, as in a car collision.
